Messages.Author: pallando
Messages.Body:
I was wondering about the upcoming anarch set:

Is the release day set?
Will there be a preview? If so when will it start?
Will WW publish a card list in time, i.e., a few days before the release?

Those who are interested can take a look at the homepage of comigimages the

open approach to new sets (Velocity just released, Survivor Series 2
upcoming).

http://www.comicimages.com/rawdeal/

I like the way they draw the attention of their customers by publishing the
full spoiler list in waves week after week.

regards

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>Another group that appreciates rarity indicators is new players.
>Getting ripped off in trades because you don't have any idea of the
>relative value of a card is a very real thing.

But would a rarity indicator really help with this? Don't forget one of the
benefits that Jyhad/VTES has over *many other games* is that it doesn't really
have power rares. It other games, yeah, it's really important to know which
card is the rare but that's because sometimes you have the cases where people
literally buy boosters just for the rare and throw away the rest. In
Jyhad/VTES, the cards are much more balanced.

If anything, the presence of a rarity indicator could further increase the
problem of getting ripped off. Sure, you won't be able to trade an Aids from
Bats for a Protected Resources, but people might get a little too comfortable.
Hey, look at this super cool Tasha Morgan card. I'll offer you it for your
Protected Resources. See, since they're both "rare," the trade is perfectly
fair!

All this comes down to a completely different issue (that of what a "fair"
trade is). For those card speculators who rely on eBay prices it wouldn't
really help either because you could still easily get ripped off *despite* the
presence of rarity indicators.

Halcyan 2

Sure, I don't expect everyone to remember every little detail, but it's really
not that hard to get "a feel" for the rarity of a card. As I mentioned before,
it's not as much of an issue in Jyhad/VTES since cards are much more balanced
(and I personally don't think it really matters whether Dramatic Upheaval is a
C or a U), but it's really not hard to be able to sift out the rares.

>As for the card list, I don't enjoy the idea of carrying around
>a card list (considering the size of this document). I think if anything,
>if rarity changes during in between sets, having the rarity on the card will
>simply indicate the rarity of that card for the set it was released in and
>this IMHO is alot better than having a list that says for such and such a
>card, it was rare in Jyhad but uncommon in CE. I mean, what's the harm
>really? From the point of view of a quality engineer, if something improves
>customer satisfaction without increased cost and decreased function, go for
>it.

But you see, the presence of rarity indicators will mean more people will rely
on them in determining a "fair" trade. You mentioned yourself that the rarity
indicator would simply indicate the rarity in that set. Thus you could have
increasing complications. What happens if you have a set with no rares (like
Dark Sovereigns). Wouldn't that distort things a bit? How many U1's would be
equal to a Tasha Morgan? And also, when you do have rarity changes in between
sets, you'd have additional problems. I could trade you Freak Drives with the
rare bug when you think they're rare. And only later on, when you opened CE
packs, would you find Freak Drives with the uncommon bug and think "what the
frell?"

Similarly, there are other things out there that might make some people happy,
but the game really doesn't need it. Take for example the issue of foil rares.
How about we just make the R1's foils, as have been done in other games? I
personally think it's a dreadful idea because foil cards wouldn't work well
with VTES IMO (plus it would probably look tacky combined with other cards). So
just like how I think we don't need foil rares (which just about every CCG has
nowadays), we similarly don't need rarity indicators.

Halcyan 2

Saying we don't need rarity indications is a bold assumption/opinion. I
assume when you say we, you are referring to yourself and select group of
people you know. I for one would find a rarity indicator on cards a useful
source of information.

>

As a general discussion, You really have to look at the POV of White Wolf
and analyze how the Fit, Form and Function of a product is affected by a
potential customer/customer request to add to a product. I mean, you can
make any arguments you want pro or con but what I comes down to is that if
WW execs are sitting there and have some research data that says "More
people will buy and play V:TES if we add rarity indicators to cards" then
those executives are going to ask the design engineers to go into a
Risk/Cost/Design analysis to see if this can be done. Of course, when the
execs find out that the Design engineers say "Adding a rarity indicator has
minimal impact on how the card works and plays, the cost to print the card
and way the card is designed", the exec's will say "Why didn't we do this
sooner? It increases sales and visibility of our product." I can't really
see anyone quiting VTES because of rarity indicator. The knowledged fans
know what there cards are worth, regardless of what is printed on a card.
It's really for the 'new customer' group and the 'existing customers that
request this functionality' group.

What happens to a set with no rares like DS? The same thing as happens now.
How many U1's would be equal to a Tasha Morgan? The answer is as always,
whatever your willing to pay/trade.
The issue with the Freak Drive? It's already happened, and there is no
rarity indicator on the card.

My point is this. Rarity indicators on cards serve to give information and
will add value to them without affecting the Fit, Form and Function of the
cards. How can WW lose by doing it if their research indicates it's
something that customers want? Basically, the answer is that a company to
remain competitive must satisfy a large number of customer groups. You
belong to one, me another, the next guy a different one from both of us,
etc. If they add value to a product to increase their market share with
mininal effect to the customer groups, then that is something they should
do.

Messages.Author: Cecil
Messages.Body:
>
> Furthermore I'd like to mention that some rarity indication on the cards.
> This would help many people a lot and doesn't hurt anybody. As far as this
> can be implemented easily. I am aware of the fact that this can't be
> implemented in Anarchs unless it is already done. Still, it would be very
> nice to have in a future expansion.
>

Rarity indicators already exist... The rare in a bloodlines pack is
the last card at the bottom. ;-)

Seriously though, rarity indicators really aren't that much of a help,
unless they are going to differentiate between 'good' and 'bad' rares.
Like Halycon said, tasha for a protected isn't a great deal, but they
are both rares.

Someone else said that unlike magic, there are no "power cards" in
VTES so you won't have trading sharks snapping them up from newbies. I
think this, while somewhat true (I have a feeling that powercards DO
exist in this game but that is for another post) misses a point. VTES
relies on community in order to have a game. In magic, or other
"dueling" games, you only need one other player. In VTES you need 3 to
play, 4 to make a real game. Getting newbies to buy cards and then
sharking the rares is going to scare off potential players and ruin
your playgroup. When a new player starts you group should encourage
her, because without that person you may be at a game night without a
4th listening to the crickets chirp.

Here's an example: When I first started playing I bought a bunch of
packs of FN and SW. In those packs I got 1 disarm and 1 abomination. A
player in my group said,"great cards... care to trade them?" I decided
that I did want to get rid of them, and he gave me a stack of cards -
I'd say 30 or 40. Several uncommons, a war ghoul, some sabbat only
vampires, a horrid form, a blood of acid, and tons of other stuff. He
loaded me up with Brujah anti and Tzimice stuff. Another player traded
me for a provision of the silisa, and gave me a stack of cards,
several of them rare. They did this because they wanted the cards from
me, but wanted to make sure that I didn't feel cheated.

So what it boils down to is that there already is a rare indicator on
cards, it is the playgroup looking over the shoulder of the new player
saying, "hey great card!"

And ultimately a rare indicator cannot be a "useful card" indicator.

I'm still looking to get rid of my mistaken identity and twisting the
knife cards. Care to trade a rare for a rare?

Cecil

Messages.Author: Snapcase
Messages.Body:
halc...@aol.com (Halcyan 2) wrote in message news:<20030407234212...@mb-cg.aol.com>...

> >Another group that appreciates rarity indicators is new players.
> >Getting ripped off in trades because you don't have any idea of the
> >relative value of a card is a very real thing.

> But would a rarity indicator really help with this? Don't forget one of the
> benefits that Jyhad/VTES has over *many other games* is that it doesn't really
> have power rares.

Yes, it would. While Jyhad has a good deal of balance (rares tend to
be good in less decks than commons), the fact remains that it still
has cards of differing rarities. New players don't like having their
rare cards traded off them for common ones. While most rare cards
aren't considered "power rares", they're still generally more
difficult to aquire than an uncommon or common card.

> It other games, yeah, it's really important to know which
> card is the rare but that's because sometimes you have the cases where people
> literally buy boosters just for the rare and throw away the rest. In
> Jyhad/VTES, the cards are much more balanced.

That has as much to do with the fact that there's no card limit as
card balance. Mentally put a 3 card limit on your decks and see if
you keep those commons you already have dozens of when you buy a
booster.

> If anything, the presence of a rarity indicator could further increase the
> problem of getting ripped off. Sure, you won't be able to trade an Aids from
> Bats for a Protected Resources, but people might get a little too comfortable.
> Hey, look at this super cool Tasha Morgan card. I'll offer you it for your
> Protected Resources. See, since they're both "rare," the trade is perfectly
> fair!

So people trading rares for rares is increasing the problem? Yes,
there are differing values among the rarities based on play value.
But that's the same in every game. The idea is to at least keep
people trading rares for rares instead of ripping newbies off
completely with the Aid from Bats trade.

> All this comes down to a completely different issue (that of what a "fair"
> trade is). For those card speculators who rely on eBay prices it wouldn't
> really help either because you could still easily get ripped off *despite* the
> presence of rarity indicators.

Auctioning is a completely different animal though (made evident by
the amount of people willing to spend >10$ for Ian Forestal). People
that rely on eBay prices already have some basis of comparing card
values. The newbie who just started playing and doesn't "do the eBay"
yet has no basis of comparing card values. Everyone's going to have a
different definition of what a "fair" trade is. The idea is that
newbies are generally thankful of a rarity indicator so they can avoid
the Aid From Bats scam.

Rarity indicators don't hurt at all and they're generally
non-intrusive. There's no reason not to have them (unless they
increase production costs in some way that I'm not aware of).

-Snapcase

I only want to detail one remaining issue before I call quits on this
thread (as it has recurred like 3 times in the last year).

Rarity indicators are NOT all about the player. While it does aid in
trade, etc. It's a great aid for the retailer that carry the VTES
product.

Of all the card games (and clix) that are sold/supported in my area (and
a good chunk of Michigan), retailers use Rarity to establish a base
price for sales of singles (of a target product). Considering the
marginal following of VTES and lack of a rarity indicator there is no
incentive for a store to push sales of individual cards.

With a rarity indicator, a store can set an arbitrary price at a glance.
Commons .10
Uncommons .50
Rares 2.00

When stores are able to recoup their cost of time and investment in a
product, that's all well and good. When a store is actually able to
turn a modest profit, they will be more likely to support/promote
tournaments and player activity.

Without retailer support & promotion, this game will continue to
function in the background regardless of WW and VEKN's exceptional
involvement.

A rarity indicator isn't going to be the entire answer on how to gain
new players, but a new player is used to having rarity indicators on
their cards as they are probably now coming in from Magic/Pokemon/etc..

Point being that an indicator is expected by newer players, and not
having one is yet another reason for them to walk away.
Plus! Having a rarity indicator would allow those mega collectors
another option on how to sort their cards :-)

That's the last I have to say in this thread.

BernieTime
Lansing, Michigan

While this statement is true, those people aren't actually 'new
players', they're 'new collectors', which is largely irrelevant to the
discussion at hand.

Besides which, I have never heard a collector select a new game to
collect based on whether or not they had to use a checklist vs. a
rarity indicator on the card. They're <ALREADY> having to use a
checklist, because their concern is not 'how rare is this card' but
rather 'have I gotten all of the cards'. To truly aid collectors with
indicators on the card, you'd need a '5 of 324' like those that appear
on purely-trading cards.

> Another group that appreciates rarity indicators is new players.
> Getting ripped off in trades because you don't have any idea of the
> relative value of a card is a very real thing.

Very true. Though a truly unscrupulous trader will still be more than
able to swap even-rarity, uneven-value cards. "I'll trade you this
Rare Praxis Seizure: Miami for that Rare Shroud of Absence!

> People wouldn't *need* a cardlist to know rarity if the indicators were
> already on the card. That's part of the point.

Yep. Don't get me wrong - I'm in full agreement that printing rarity
on the card would not be a bad thing. I'm just commenting that it
would in no way suddenly turn the game into a best-seller
greatest-product-since-sliced-bread item either.

I mean, let's face it. Jyhad is not the simplest game in the world,
nor the quickest to learn. New players have a harder time adjusting to
the complexity of game play than to trying to figure out card rarity,
especially when there exist many sources to have the rarities spelled
out (the website, the newsgroup, scrye magazine, and so on).

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Halcyan 2 wrote:

> But would a rarity indicator really help with this?

(avoiding getting ripped off)--it might help, and it certainly can't hurt.

Mind you, I'm not like wildly pro rariy indicators or anything--if they were
on the cards in an unobtrusive way (like changing the color of the already
existing expansion symbol), I wouldn't be offended, and they certainly might
be useful at some point. This being said, I can't for the life of me see a
valid reason to not include them. Again, if they never were implimented, I'd
be just as happy as not, but I can't see why they wouldn't be implimented.

> If anything, the presence of a rarity indicator could further increase the
> problem of getting ripped off.

Oh, that's just silly. Having more information can never hurt. Knowing that
a card is rare gives you an idea of its relative value. Mind you, value can
mean many things to many people, but generally speaking, in a given set, a
rare is worth a rare. Sure, some rares are really valuable and some are
total ass, but knowing that a card is a rare as opposed to a common is
*never* going to be detrimental.

> Sure, you won't be able to trade an Aids from
> Bats for a Protected Resources, but people might get a little too comfortable.
> Hey, look at this super cool Tasha Morgan card. I'll offer you it for your
> Protected Resources. See, since they're both "rare," the trade is perfectly
> fair!

How is that any different than having rarity lists on the internet? Should
they do away with those?

Yes, Tasha Morgan is ass compared to a Protected Resources in many
senses--Tasha Morgan has, generally speaking, less play value than PR; There
are *many* more Tasha Morgans in circulation than PRs. But if someone is
trying to complete a CE set, and they really need a Tasha and have an extra
PR, it seems likely that both parties are getting a good deal.

> All this comes down to a completely different issue (that of what a "fair"
> trade is). For those card speculators who rely on eBay prices it wouldn't
> really help either because you could still easily get ripped off *despite* the
> presence of rarity indicators.

None of this at all supports the idea that rarity indicators would be
detrimental. At all. Sure, they might not be incredibly useful. Or
particularly necessary. And they might offend the "elitist" mindset of some,
but there is no significant reason that adding them is bad.

Again--I don't really care one way or the other, but I can't really see how
adding them would be bad.

figure 1: rarity 1,2, or 3
figure 2: rarity 2, 3, or 4
figure 3: rarity 3, 4, or 5 (or 6? unique?)
figure 4: rarity 1, 2, 3, or 4

figures are mostly the uniques and LEs though - they have silver and
